trace_80.severe_distance_20: 20/20 connector-synthesis lane-count mismatch (inc 2-4 lanes vs con 1 lane), outer->inner mapping, ref-coincident. FIRST_DIVERGENCE_STAGE=Stage3/7 connector synthesis.
trace_80.severe_angle_20: mixed: width mismatch (3.25/3.0/3.75 vs 3.5) + lane-count mismatch + genuine heading discontinuity on equal-count equal-width links (e.g. j5/c1 96deg, j122/c1 90deg). FIRST_DIVERGENCE_STAGE=Stage7 width policy OR Stage3/5 geometry.
trace_80.both_20: equal-count width mismatch with ~180deg heading flips (wrong connecting-road orientation / reversed geometry) + lane-count mismatch cases. FIRST_DIVERGENCE_STAGE=Stage7 width policy OR Stage8 mapping/geometry.
trace_80.passing_20: equal-count inner->inner with small width delta (0.125m, below threshold) pass; multi-lane connector j1/c4 (2v2) passes at 0.0. Confirms inner->inner + harmonized width is the passing shape.
trace_80.method: final XODR laneLink read -> lane link builder semantics -> junction graph (connection/contactPoint) -> road link builder (predecessor/successor) -> SUMO conversion inheritance (outer->inner signature differs from match_by_direction inner-first) -> OSM lane-count authority

gap048_correlation.interpretation: Same generator deficiency (single-lane connectors vs multi-lane incident roads) produces two complementary symptoms: WRONG laneLink (GAP-026 outer->inner mispair, 830 pruned) vs MISSING laneLink (GAP-048 no-candidate outer lanes left unwired). Low direct lane overlap (9.6%) is expected — they are opposite outcomes of one cause. The 115 missing-candidate cases partially stem from the same deficiency; the 261 ambiguous forks are genuine topology requiring explicit residuals.
